status.en: 18 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Mogadishu, Baidoa and Puntland.
status.nb: 18 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Mogadishu, Baidoa og Puntland.

summary.en: Al-Shabaab continues to launch large-scale attacks on Somali army units, including a deadly convoy ambush that killed many soldiers and a mortar strike in Puntland that killed three civilians and wounded seven. Fighting erupted near Baidoa as the army advanced on Burhakabo, while a major battle near Buurhakaba district resulted in heavy casualties on both sides, with the army reporting 75 al-Shabaab fighters killed. Somalia denied that Turkish F‑16 aircraft struck its own positions during the clashes. The conflict produced 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Al-Shabaab fortsetter å gjennomføre store angrep på somaliske hærstyrker, inkludert et dødelig bakholdsangrep på en konvoi som drepte mange soldater og et morterangrep i Puntland som drepte tre sivile og såret sju. Kamp brøt ut nær Baidoa da hæren rykket frem mot Burhakabo, mens et stort slag i Buurhakaba-distriktet førte til tunge tap på begge sider, med hæren som rapporterte 75 al-Shabaab-krigere drept. Somalia benektet at tyrkiske F‑16‑fly rammet egne posisjoner under kampene. Konflikten førte til 2 284 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.extract: The ongoing phase of the Somali Civil War began in 2009 and is concentrated in southern and central Somalia, primarily between the forces of the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), assisted by African Union peacekeeping forces, and the Islamist militant group al-Shabaab, which pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda in 2012.

posts.author: The Associated Press
posts.text: Islamic extremist militants killed at least 20 Somali soldiers in an ambush, a military officer who survived the attack said, as the government acknowledged damage to military vehicles but disclosed no troop casualties. The al-Qaida-linked al-Shabab group claimed responsibility for Monday's attack.
